findings.passage: Let us return elections to the generations of registered Pennsylvania voters who have gone to the polls with only their signatures. It is what we expect. It is what should be.
findings.note: Press release after the Commonwealth Court struck down the 2012 photo ID law; she says voters should return to signing in at the polls, and says there is very little fraud.

findings.passage: The petitioners did a great job proving there is very little fraud in Philadelphia and throughout the state.
findings.note: Same release; she cites court evidence on the amount of in-person fraud.

findings.passage: I’ve been confident all along that the courts would see the serious flaws and dubious reasoning behind voter ID,
findings.note: Statement on the Commonwealth Court order keeping a soft roll-out, where voters are asked for ID but not required to show it.

findings.passage: For months I’ve been hearing from frustrated seniors, students and others who didn’t know what the requirements were and the requirements kept changing,
findings.note: Same release; she describes voter confusion about ID rules in her district.

findings.passage: Creating barriers to prevent the disabled from voicing their grievances with their government, either inside the Capitol or inside the polling place, has become a priority with the legislature’s Republican majority and the current administration,
findings.note: Reaction to Senate passage of House Bill 934 (photo ID at polls); the release says her amendment to exempt voters with disabilities was rejected. Quoted text names a party, copied verbatim as her words.
